questions.why: A level platform at least 30 inches in every dimension, with guards, is required on each service side.

questions.q: Guards are required when rooftop equipment needing service is within what distance of a roof edge that is more than 30 in above the surface below?
questions.why: Equipment or roof hatches within 10 ft of such an edge require guards.

questions.q: Rooftop equipment guards must have a top at least how high above the adjacent surface?
questions.why: Guards must be at least 42 inches high and extend 30 inches beyond each end of the equipment.

questions.q: In a residential garage, a gas water heater's ignition source must be at least how high above the floor?
questions.why: Ignition sources in garages must be elevated at least 18 inches above the floor.

questions.q: Unless protected from vehicle impact, appliances in a private garage must have a minimum clearance above the floor of:
questions.why: Private garage appliances need 6 ft of clearance above the floor unless protected from impact.

questions.q: In a public or repair garage, appliances must be installed at least how high above the floor (unless protected from impact)?
questions.why: Public garage appliances must be at least 8 ft above the floor.

questions.q: A condensing unit set on a pad at grade must be supported at least how far above the adjoining grade?
questions.why: At-grade equipment sits on a slab at least 3 in above grade or is suspended at least 6 in above grade.

questions.q: Which is a permitted location for a fuel-fired appliance under the prohibited-location rule?
c: A storage closet, natural draft furnace
A bedroom, natural draft water heater
A toilet room, Category I furnace
questions.why: Direct-vent appliances are an exception to the prohibition on sleeping rooms, bathrooms, toilet rooms and storage closets.

questions.q: The NEC requires a 125-V service receptacle within what distance of rooftop HVAC equipment?
questions.why: A 15- or 20-A, 125-V receptacle is required within 25 ft of HVAC equipment on the same level.

questions.q: Required heating systems must be able to maintain what indoor temperature 3 ft above the floor on the design heating day?
questions.why: The IMC requires capacity to maintain at least 68 F at 3 ft above the floor.

questions.q: What is the minimum internal diameter of a condensate drain line from a single cooling coil?
questions.why: Condensate drains must be at least 3/4 in ID and may not decrease in size.

questions.q: Condensate drains from units totaling 30 tons are manifolded together. The minimum common drain size is:
questions.why: Over 20 to 40 tons requires a 1-inch condensate line.

questions.q: Manifolded condensate drains serving 100 tons of equipment require a minimum pipe size of:
questions.why: Over 90 to 125 tons requires 1-1/2 inch pipe.

questions.q: An auxiliary drain pan under an attic air handler must be at least how deep?
questions.why: Auxiliary pans must be at least 1-1/2 inches deep.

questions.q: An auxiliary drain pan must be larger than the unit or coil by at least:
questions.why: The pan must be at least 3 inches larger than the unit or coil in width and length.

questions.q: A galvanized steel auxiliary drain pan must be at least what thickness?
questions.why: Galvanized auxiliary pans must be at least 0.0236 in (No. 24 gage).

questions.q: Water-level detection devices used to shut off equipment when a condensate drain clogs must conform to:
questions.why: Water-level shutoff devices must conform to UL 508.

questions.q: On a down-flow unit with no room for a secondary pan, where must the water-level monitoring device be installed?
c: In the drain line outside the unit
questions.why: For down-flow units, the device goes inside the primary drain pan; external or in-line devices are not allowed.

questions.q: Condensate drains for ductless mini-split equipment must have:
c: An inline check valve or a trap
questions.why: Mini-split condensate drains need an inline check valve or a trap.

questions.q: Natural ventilation of a space requires openable exterior openings of at least what percent of the floor area?
questions.why: The minimum openable area to the outdoors is 4 percent of the floor area.

questions.q: Using Vbz = Rp x Pz + Ra x Az, what outdoor air is required for a 1,000 sq ft office with 5 people (Rp = 5 cfm, Ra = 0.06 cfm/sq ft)?
A dwelling bathroom exhaust fan that runs intermittently must provide at least:
questions.why: Bathrooms require 50 cfm intermittent or 20 cfm continuous.

questions.q: A dwelling kitchen exhaust that runs intermittently must provide at least:
questions.why: Kitchens require 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous.

questions.q: Using 0.01 x floor area + 7.5 x (bedrooms + 1), the continuous whole-house ventilation for a 2,000 sq ft, 3-bedroom home is:
Whole-house mechanical ventilation is required when a dwelling's blower door test is below:
questions.why: Dwellings under 5 air changes per hour at 50 Pa must have whole-house mechanical ventilation.

questions.q: A mechanical outdoor-air intake must be at least how far horizontally from a hazardous or noxious contaminant source such as a plumbing vent?
questions.why: Intakes must be at least 10 ft horizontally from contaminant sources.

questions.q: In a public toilet room with an intermittently operated exhaust fan, the exhaust rate per water closet or urinal is:
questions.why: Public toilet rooms need 70 cfm per fixture intermittent or 50 cfm continuous.

questions.q: A residential bath exhaust outlet must terminate at least how far from a mechanical air intake (unless 3 ft above it)?
questions.why: Exhaust openings need 10 ft from mechanical intakes, or 3 ft vertical separation above them.

questions.q: Environmental air exhaust (such as toilet exhaust) must terminate at least how far from property lines?
questions.why: Environmental exhaust must be 3 ft from property lines and operable openings, and 10 ft from mechanical intakes.

questions.q: Which is an acceptable termination for a bathroom exhaust fan?
c: Into the attic near a gable vent
questions.why: Exhaust must discharge directly outdoors, not into attics, soffits, ridge vents or crawl spaces.

questions.q: The maximum developed length of a domestic dryer exhaust duct, before fitting deductions, is:
questions.why: The limit is 35 ft from the transition duct connection to the outlet, reduced for fittings.

questions.q: How much must be deducted from the dryer duct length for each 4-in-radius mitered 90-degree elbow?
questions.why: A 4-in-radius mitered 90-degree elbow counts as 5 ft of duct.

questions.q: A dryer duct has two 4-in-radius mitered 90s and one mitered 45. What is the maximum straight duct allowed?
The dryer transition duct must be listed to UL 2158A and may be no longer than:
questions.why: Transition ducts are limited to a single length of 8 ft and may not be concealed.

questions.q: When a dryer duct's equivalent length exceeds 35 ft, a label stating the length must be placed within what distance of the duct connection?
questions.why: The permanent label or tag goes within 6 ft of the exhaust duct connection.

questions.q: Screws used at dryer exhaust duct joints may protrude into the duct no more than:
questions.why: Fasteners may not protrude more than 1/8 inch into the duct, to limit lint buildup.

questions.q: Dryer exhaust must terminate at least how far from openings into the building (absent other manufacturer instructions)?
questions.why: Dryer terminations must be at least 3 ft from openings, and screens are not allowed.

questions.q: A domestic range hood requires makeup air when it can exhaust more than:
questions.why: Hoods over 400 cfm need makeup air at about the same rate with an interlocked damper.

questions.q: The minimum slope for a horizontal grease duct 50 ft long serving a Type I hood is:
questions.why: Horizontal grease ducts slope at least 1/4 in per ft; runs over 75 ft need 1 in per ft.

questions.q: Grease duct systems serving Type I hoods must maintain a minimum air velocity of:
questions.why: The minimum grease duct velocity is 500 feet per minute.

questions.q: A steel grease duct must be at least what thickness?
questions.why: Grease ducts must be 16 gage steel or 18 gage stainless steel.

questions.q: Without a listed reduction, a grease duct needs what clearance to combustible construction?
questions.why: Grease ducts need 18 in to combustibles and 3 in to noncombustibles.

questions.q: A canopy-type commercial kitchen hood must overhang the cooking appliances on open sides by at least:
questions.why: Canopy hoods must extend at least 6 inches beyond the appliances on all open sides.

questions.q: The lowest edge of grease filters above an exposed charcoal or charbroil fire must be at least:
questions.why: Filters must be 3.5 ft above charcoal/charbroil fires, 2 ft above exposed flame, 0.5 ft otherwise.

questions.q: A rooftop grease exhaust outlet must discharge at least how high above the roof surface?
questions.why: Rooftop grease duct terminations discharge at least 40 inches above the roof.

questions.q: Flexible air connectors are limited in length to:
questions.why: Flexible air connectors may be no longer than 14 ft and may not pass through walls, floors or ceilings.

questions.q: Gypsum board may be used to form air ducts only when:
c: It carries supply air under 140 F
It carries return air not over 125 F
questions.why: Gypsum shafts are limited to return air at 125 F or less, with surfaces above dew point.

questions.q: Duct coverings and linings must have a maximum flame spread index of 25 and a maximum smoke-developed index of:
questions.why: Coverings and linings are limited to flame spread 25 and smoke-developed 50.

questions.q: Tape listed for sealing flexible air ducts carries which marking?
questions.why: UL 181B covers flex duct closures; tapes are marked 181B-FX and mastics 181B-M.

questions.q: A stud wall cavity used as a plenum in a building may carry:
questions.why: Stud cavity and joist space plenums are limited to return air and may not serve more than one floor level.

questions.q: Duct smoke detectors are required in the return air of systems with a design capacity greater than:
questions.why: Return air smoke detection is required above 2,000 cfm, upstream of filters and outdoor air connections.

questions.q: A fire damper installed in a 2-hour fire-resistance-rated wall must have a minimum rating of:
questions.why: Assemblies rated less than 3 hours need 1-1/2-hour fire dampers.

questions.q: Fire damper access points must be labeled with letters at least how tall?
questions.why: Labels reading FIRE DAMPER, SMOKE DAMPER or FIRE/SMOKE DAMPER must have letters at least 1/2 inch high.

questions.q: Ducts penetrating the wall between a house and its attached garage must be at least:
c: No. 30 gage steel with no openings
No. 26 gage steel with no openings into the garage
No. 22 gage steel with a fire damper
questions.why: Garage ducts and penetrating ducts must be at least 26 gage steel and have no openings into the garage.

questions.q: Under the 2021 IECC, a 6-inch supply duct in a vented attic must be insulated to at least:
questions.why: Ducts 3 in and larger outside conditioned space need R-8.

questions.q: What is the maximum total duct leakage for a 2,000 sq ft home tested post-construction under the 2021 IECC?
questions.why: 4.0 cfm per 100 sq ft x 20 = 80 cfm at 25 Pa.

questions.q: Using the standard method, how much room volume is needed for appliances totaling 140,000 Btu/h to use indoor combustion air?
questions.why: 50 cu ft per 1,000 Btu/h x 140 = 7,000 cu ft.

questions.q: Two indoor openings connecting rooms on the same story for combustion air must each be at least:
c: 1 sq in per 1,000 Btu/h, minimum 100 sq in
questions.why: Each opening needs 1 sq in per 1,000 Btu/h of total input, but not less than 100 sq in.

questions.q: Two outdoor combustion air openings connected through horizontal ducts must each provide:
questions.why: Horizontal ducts require 1 sq in per 2,000 Btu/h; direct or vertical ducts 1 per 4,000.

questions.q: A 120,000 Btu/h appliance uses two outdoor openings through vertical ducts. Each opening must have a free area of at least:
questions.why: 120,000 / 4,000 = 30 sq in per opening.

questions.q: A single permanent outdoor combustion air opening must provide at least:
questions.why: One opening needs 1 sq in per 3,000 Btu/h, located within 12 in of the top.

questions.q: Mechanical combustion air systems must supply at least:
questions.why: Mechanical combustion air must be at least 0.35 cfm per 1,000 Btu/h, interlocked with the appliance.

questions.q: When louver free area is unknown, metal louvers are assumed to have a free area of:
questions.why: Metal louvers are assumed 75 percent free area; wood louvers 25 percent.

questions.q: A condensing furnace whose vent operates under positive pressure is classified as Category:
questions.why: Category IV appliances have positive vent pressure and produce condensate.

questions.q: Vent connectors must slope upward toward the vent or chimney at a minimum of:
questions.why: Connectors must rise at least 1/4 inch per foot with no dips or sags.

questions.q: With a 20 ft high gas vent, the maximum horizontal length of a single-wall connector is:
questions.why: Single-wall connectors are limited to 75 percent of vent height: 0.75 x 20 = 15 ft.

questions.q: A single-wall connector from a listed draft-hood appliance needs what clearance to combustibles?
questions.why: Single-wall connectors on listed draft-hood appliances need 6 inches unless the listing says otherwise.

questions.q: A chimney must extend at least 3 ft above the roof penetration and at least how far above any part of the building within 10 ft?
questions.why: This is the 3-2-10 rule: 3 ft above the roof, 2 ft above anything within 10 ft.

questions.q: A Type B gas vent must terminate at least how far above the highest connected draft hood or flue collar?
questions.why: Type B and L vents need 5 ft of vertical height; B-W vents need 12 ft.

questions.q: A mechanical draft vent terminal must be at least how far above any door, operable window or gravity air inlet (if not 4 ft below or beside it)?
questions.why: Power vent terminals must be 4 ft below, 4 ft horizontally from, or 1 ft above such openings.

questions.q: A direct-vent appliance rated 40,000 Btu/h needs what minimum terminal clearance from an air opening into the building?
questions.why: Over 10,000 to 50,000 Btu/h requires 9 inches.

questions.q: Gas piping must be tested at 1-1/2 times the maximum working pressure, but never less than:
questions.why: The minimum gas test pressure is 3 psig regardless of design pressure.

questions.q: What is the minimum duration of a gas piping pressure test?
questions.why: The test must last at least 10 minutes.

questions.q: Which test medium is prohibited for gas piping tests?
questions.why: Oxygen may never be used; air, nitrogen, CO2 or inert gas are allowed.

questions.q: An appliance gas shutoff valve must be in the same room and within what distance of the appliance?
questions.why: Shutoff valves must be accessible, in the same room and within 6 ft.

questions.q: The maximum overall length of a flexible gas appliance connector is:
questions.why: Connectors are limited to 6 ft, one per appliance, and may not pass through walls or floors.

questions.q: Which appliance is exempt from the sediment trap requirement?
questions.why: Ranges, clothes dryers, illuminating appliances, decorative vented appliances and outdoor grills are exempt.

questions.q: The bonding jumper for a CSST gas system must be at least:
questions.why: CSST bonding jumpers must be 6 AWG copper or equivalent and no longer than 75 ft.

questions.q: General underground gas piping must be buried at least how deep?
questions.why: Underground gas piping needs 12 in of cover; individual lines to outdoor grills or lights may be 8 in.

questions.q: Gas piping bored through a stud less than 1-1/2 in from its face requires a steel shield plate at least:
questions.why: Shield plates must be at least No. 16 gage and extend 4 in beyond the member.

questions.q: Horizontal 1/2-inch steel gas pipe must be supported at intervals of no more than:
questions.why: 1/2-in steel pipe is supported every 6 ft; 3/4 and 1 in every 8 ft; 1-1/4 in and larger every 10 ft.

questions.q: Which statement about propane is correct?
c: It has about 1,000 Btu per cubic foot
It is heavier than air and collects in low areas
It is tabulated in CFH in IFGC sizing tables
questions.why: Propane has a specific gravity near 1.5, so it sinks and collects in low spots.

questions.q: Using about 1,000 Btu per cubic foot, how much natural gas does a 100,000 Btu/h furnace need?
questions.why: 100,000 / 1,000 = 100 cubic feet per hour.

questions.q: Hydronic piping must be hydrostatically tested at 1-1/2 times design pressure, but not less than:
questions.why: Hydronic tests are at 1.5 x design pressure, minimum 100 psi, held at least 15 minutes.

questions.q: A 10 GPM hydronic loop with a 20 F temperature drop delivers about:
questions.ref: Q = 500 x GPM x delta T

questions.q: How much pressure does a 25 ft column of water exert at its base?
questions.why: 25 x 0.433 = about 10.8 psi.

questions.q: What control is required on steam and hot water boilers to shut down the burner if water drops too low?
questions.why: Boilers need a low-water cutoff (forced-circulation coil boilers may use a flow switch).

questions.q: An ASME Section IV low-pressure steam boiler operates at no more than:
questions.why: Low-pressure steam heating boilers are limited to 15 psi; hot water boilers to 160 psi and 250 F.

questions.q: R-454B and R-32 are classified in which ASHRAE 34 safety group?
questions.why: Both are lower-toxicity, lower-flammability (2L) refrigerants.

questions.q: In a refrigerant safety classification such as B1, the letter B indicates:
questions.why: A = lower toxicity, B = higher toxicity; the number shows flammability.

questions.q: Machinery room emergency ventilation is Q = 100 x the square root of G. For a system holding 100 lb, Q is:
questions.why: 100 x square root of 100 = 100 x 10 = 1,000 cfm.

questions.q: Outdoor refrigerant access ports must be fitted with:
questions.why: Outdoor access ports need locking, tamper-resistant caps or other security.

questions.q: Which gas may be used to pressure test field-erected refrigerant piping?
questions.why: Use dry nitrogen or another inert gas; oxygen, air and combustible gases are prohibited.

questions.q: Under EPA's Technology Transitions rule, new residential split AC systems manufactured from January 1, 2025 must use refrigerant with a GWP below:
questions.why: The limit for residential and light commercial AC and heat pumps is GWP below 700.

questions.q: Under 40 CFR 82.157, the leak rate that triggers repair for a comfort cooling appliance with 50 lb or more of R-22 is:
questions.why: Comfort cooling is 10 percent; commercial refrigeration 20; industrial process 30.

questions.q: The leak rate threshold for commercial refrigeration appliances with 50 lb or more is:
questions.why: Commercial refrigeration (retail food and cold storage) triggers repair at 20 percent per year.

questions.q: After a comfort cooling appliance exceeds its leak rate, leaks must normally be repaired within:
questions.why: Repairs are due within 30 days, or 120 days if an industrial process shutdown is needed.

questions.q: A follow-up verification test must be done within how many days of a successful initial verification test?
questions.why: The follow-up verification test is due within 10 days.

questions.q: Appliances that leak 125 percent or more of their full charge in a calendar year must be reported to EPA by:
questions.why: Chronically leaking appliance reports are due March 1 of the following year.

questions.q: Using the annualizing method, 10 lb added to a 100 lb system 73 days after the last addition gives a leak rate of:
questions.why: 10/100 x 365/73 x 100 = 50 percent per year.

questions.q: Before disposal, a high-pressure appliance with less than 200 lb of charge must be evacuated to:
questions.why: High-pressure appliances under 200 lb require 0 inches of mercury.

questions.q: Using recovery equipment made after November 15, 1993, a medium-pressure appliance with 200 lb or more must be evacuated to:
questions.why: Medium-pressure 200 lb or more requires 15 in Hg; under 200 lb requires 10 in Hg.

questions.q: The required evacuation level for a low-pressure (R-123) chiller is:
questions.why: Low-pressure appliances must be evacuated to 25 mm Hg absolute.

questions.q: Recovery equipment made after November 15, 1993 used on a small appliance with a running compressor must recover:
questions.why: 90 percent with the compressor running, 80 percent if not, or evacuate to 4 in Hg.

questions.q: System-dependent recovery equipment may not be used on appliances with a full charge of more than:
questions.why: System-dependent equipment is limited to appliances with 15 lb or less.

questions.q: Which of these is a major repair under EPA rules?
questions.why: Removing the compressor, condenser, evaporator or auxiliary coil is a major repair.

questions.q: Under EPA definitions, R-134a is used in what type of appliance?
questions.why: R-134a and R-12 are medium-pressure refrigerants (45 to 170 psia at 104 F).

questions.q: What is the passing score for a closed-book EPA 608 Type II exam?
questions.why: Closed-book tests require 70 percent; Type I mail-in tests require 84 percent.

questions.q: The passing score for a Type I EPA 608 test given in mail-in format is:
questions.why: Mail-in Type I tests require 84 percent.

questions.q: How many questions are on a Universal EPA 608 certification exam?
questions.why: Universal is 100 questions: 25 Core plus 25 each for Types I, II and III.

questions.q: How long is an EPA Section 608 technician certification valid?
questions.why: Section 608 certification currently does not expire.

questions.q: Since January 1, 2018, the EPA refrigerant sales restriction also applies to:
questions.why: The sales restriction expanded to non-exempt substitutes like R-410A and R-134a.

questions.q: Reclaimed refrigerant must meet the purity standard of:
questions.why: Reclaimers process refrigerant to Appendix A purity, based on AHRI 700; AHRI 740 is for recovery equipment.

questions.q: Before used refrigerant can be sold to a new owner for use as refrigerant, it must be:
questions.why: Used refrigerant changing ownership must be reclaimed by a certified reclaimer.

questions.q: Which refrigerant may be vented in a commercial or industrial process refrigeration system without violating Section 608?
questions.why: Ammonia in commercial/industrial process refrigeration and absorption units is an exempt substitute.

questions.q: A scrap recycler accepting a refrigerator without recovering the refrigerant itself must obtain a signed statement listing:
c: The recoverer's name and address and the recovery date
The technician's certification card number only
questions.why: The statement must give the name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant and the date.

questions.q: Refillable recovery cylinders are identified by which colors?
questions.why: Recovery cylinders are gray with a yellow top (shoulder).

questions.q: How often must refillable DOT recovery cylinders be hydrostatically retested?
questions.why: Recovery cylinders are retested every 5 years and stamped with the test date.

questions.q: Starting January 1, 2026, EPA's HFC leak repair requirements apply to appliances with at least how much refrigerant?
questions.why: The ER&R rule covers appliances with 15 lb or more of HFC with GWP above 53.

questions.q: A low-pressure chiller's rupture disc is typically set at 15 psig, so leak-test pressure should not exceed:
questions.why: Raise pressure no higher than 10 psig to stay below the rupture disc setting.

questions.q: In what state does refrigerant leave the compressor?
questions.why: The compressor discharges high-pressure, high-temperature superheated vapor.

questions.q: The condenser saturation temperature is 110 F and the liquid line is 100 F. What is the subcooling?
questions.why: Subcooling = 110 - 100 = 10 F.

questions.q: In a TXV, which pressure acts to open the valve?
questions.why: Bulb pressure opens the valve; evaporator and spring pressure close it.

questions.q: High superheat combined with low subcooling most likely indicates:
questions.why: Both readings point to an undercharged system.

questions.q: At 100 percent relative humidity, how do dry-bulb, wet-bulb and dew point compare?
questions.why: Saturated air has equal dry-bulb, wet-bulb and dew point temperatures.

questions.q: How many grains of moisture equal one pound of water?
questions.why: There are 7,000 grains in a pound.

questions.q: A system removes 18,000 Btu/h sensible out of 24,000 Btu/h total. What is the sensible heat ratio?
Using Q = 0.68 x CFM x delta grains, what latent load is removed by 1,000 CFM with a 20-grain drop?
questions.ref: Q = 0.68 x CFM x delta grains

questions.q: Using Q = 4.5 x CFM x delta h, what is the total load for 1,000 CFM with an enthalpy change of 6 Btu/lb?
questions.ref: Q = 4.5 x CFM x delta h

questions.q: About how much airflow does a 3.5-ton air conditioner need at 400 CFM per ton?
800 CFM flows through a 12 in x 8 in duct. What is the air velocity?
A fan's speed is increased from 1,000 to 1,200 RPM. Its static pressure changes by a factor of:
questions.why: Static pressure varies with speed squared: 1.2 squared = 1.44.

questions.q: If fan speed increases by 20 percent, the brake horsepower increases by a factor of about:
questions.why: Horsepower varies with speed cubed: 1.2 cubed = 1.728.

questions.q: A 10 kW electric heat strip produces approximately:
Supply static is +0.30 in w.c. and return static is -0.20 in w.c. What is the total external static pressure?
questions.why: Add the magnitudes: 0.30 + 0.20 = 0.50 in w.c.

questions.q: Discharge is 250 psig and suction is 70 psig. What is the compression ratio?
On an HVAC nameplate, which value sets the largest breaker or fuse permitted?
questions.why: MOCP is the maximum overcurrent protection; MCA sizes the conductors.

questions.q: Under the NEC, 'within sight' of AC equipment means visible and no more than:
questions.why: A disconnect within sight must be visible and not more than 50 ft away.

questions.q: Which thermostat terminal normally energizes the condensing unit contactor?
questions.why: Y calls for cooling and energizes the compressor contactor; G runs the indoor fan.

questions.q: What is the DOE 2023 minimum efficiency for a 3-ton split air conditioner installed in Tennessee (Southeast region)?
questions.why: In the Southeast, split AC under 45,000 Btu/h needs 14.3 SEER2.

questions.q: The national 2023 minimum for a split-system heat pump is 14.3 SEER2 and:
questions.why: Split heat pumps require 14.3 SEER2 and 7.5 HSPF2.

questions.q: A 36,000 Btu/h air conditioner draws 3,000 W at rated conditions. Its EER is:
What indoor design temperatures does the IECC set for residential load calculations?
questions.why: Interior design conditions are 72 F for heating and 75 F for cooling.
